findings.title: EventBus abstraction may not earn its keep for V1's 2-3 explicit hooks
findings.description: U6 creates `src/engine/runtime/EventBus.ts` as a TypedEmitter pub/sub system so scene hooks can subscribe to state transitions via event names (`on('task:triggered', callback)`). However, R15 explicitly scopes V1 to 2-3 explicit function hooks and U7's `restaurant/hooks.ts` demonstrates hooks as directly exported functions (`onBeforeDialogue(npcId, nodeId, ctx)`), not event subscribers. The EventBus adds an indirection layer for a consumer pattern that V1 does not use. If the EventBus is intended for internal engine communication, the plan should state that explicitly.
findings.evidence: Plan U6 describes a TypedEmitter pattern where scene hooks subscribe to state transitions by event name. Plan U7 uses direct functions such as `onBeforeDialogue(npcId, nodeId, ctx)`. R15 limits V1 to 2-3 explicit function hooks and defers a DSL. No other EventBus consumer is described.
findings.recommendation: Either drop EventBus and have SessionMachine call the 2-3 hook functions directly, or explicitly document the internal engine consumers that justify EventBus.

findings.title: SceneLoader + SceneEngine split may be premature for V1's single-scene scope
findings.description: U7 creates both `SceneLoader.ts`, which validates configuration, builds the voxel world, places NPC meshes, and starts the state machine, and a `SceneEngine` facade in `src/index.ts` exposing `register()`, `activate()`, and `getActiveScene()`. With one hard-coded V1 restaurant scene, this separation adds indirection without a clear immediate payoff.
findings.evidence: Plan U7 gives SceneLoader the full scene-loading sequence and gives SceneEngine three public methods. V1 contains one hard-coded restaurant scene, while multi-scene switching is deferred.
findings.recommendation: Consider folding SceneLoader logic directly into SceneEngine for V1. Introduce the separation in V2 when unloading/switching scenes and retaining per-scene scoring context make the SRP split more valuable.

findings.title: Separate server package.json/tsconfig adds overhead for a small proxy
findings.description: The backend proxy has only a few source files but receives its own `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, and dependency management. This is a standard separation of browser and server concerns, but it creates some overhead at V1 scale.
findings.evidence: U1 creates `server/package.json`, `server/tsconfig.json`, and `server/src/index.ts`; U5 creates the ASR and intent proxy routes. The routes mainly receive a request, validate it, and forward it to the configured provider.
findings.recommendation: A single root package with a `server:dev` script would also be viable. If the separate package is retained, document it as a deliberate architecture choice.

summary.requirements_coverage: All 19 requirements (R1-R19) are covered by implementation units
summary.completeness_gaps: None — error paths, edge cases, and degradation strategies are appropriately specified for V1 scope
